name: desire to be perceived a certain way
description: Wanting to be seen with (or without) certain characteristics in a particular social context.
perceptions: It's important to be perceived well by a certain person or social group.
I want to show a particular characteristic that I think they care about.
I want to avoid showing any characteristic that they might not like.
examples: Wanting to be seen as nice, tough, competent, helpful, etc.
Wanting to avoid looking weak, dumb, etc.

guidance.description: There's nothing wrong with trying to manage your social perception - we all do it all the time simply by living in the world. But it's worth understanding that signaling strongly for one group is likely to lower your status with other groups. If you feel trapped by the need to conform in certain ways, it may help to consider which actions are for yourself and which are for the group.

variations.name: desire to conform
variations.description: Wanting to be seen with certain characteristics that align with the expectations of a particular social group.
perceptions: It's important to be perceived well by a certain social group.
I want to show a particular characteristic that I think they generally display.
I want to avoid showing any characteristic that they don't generally display.
examples: Wearing a sports team logo to the stadium.
Wearing a clothing style to fit with the group.

links: desire to be perceived a certain way
comparisons.description: Aligning with perceived social expectation is a very common way people want to be perceived.

guidance.description: Conformity doesn't happen in every situation. Some people might resist conformity while being more susceptible to these influences in others.

variations.name: desire to differentiate
variations.description: Wanting to be seen with certain characteristics that make you stand out against the expectations of a particular social group.
perceptions: It's important to be perceived well by a certain social group.
But it's also important for me to be a little different than others.
examples: Taking an unpopular stance on a topic.

links: desire to be perceived a certain way
comparisons.description: People often want to have a small harmless difference in the way they present themselves to the social group. In more individualistic societies, the differences get larger, with elaborate tattoos, unusual hairstyles, etc. In some groups, minor differences may be required to gain social status. It's ironic to conform by sticking out.

guidance.description: Focusing on your own individuality doesn’t mean you have to throw all the rules and social conventions out the window.

comparisons.description: Wanting to be perceived in a certain way is the specific strategy we have for holding or gaining status with a particular group.

commentaries.quote: One of the most paradoxical aspects of human behavior, if you ask me, is the universally felt need for freedom to be yourself and the simultaneous tendency to conform to your environment. Between making your own choices and doing what ‘everyone else’ does. That paradox creates a tension that many people struggle with.

Conformity is not inherently positive or negative. When conformity occurs because of fear, concern for one’s social standing, or has dangerous consequences, it may be seen as negative. However, conformity that protects the overall well-being of the group—mutually deciding to respect private property, for instance—can help societies succeed.
It is no measure of health to be well adjusted to a profoundly sick society.

There is a definite need for conformity in any society.  I conform to social norms every time that I get in my car and drive on the correct side of the road, obeying the speed limits and using my turn signals.
All progress has resulted from people who took unpopular positions.
To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
